newsitem.title: CANADA: BANK OF CANADA SAW SIGNIFICANT SLACK IN ECONOMY.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF CANADA SAW SIGNIFICANT SLACK IN ECONOMY.

text.p: Canada's economy is still dealing with a "significant margin" of slack despite strong growth in the first quarter, Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said at the bank's June 18 board meeting.

"As there is still a significant margin of unused capacity in the economy, the bank expects the trend of inflation to stay in the lower half of the one to three percent inflation-control target range for the balance of 1997," minutes of the meeting released on Wednesday say.
Canada's gross domestic prodcut rose by 3.4 percent in the first quarter, measured at annual rates.
The board said it expected growth in the second quarter to be strong too, remaining well above the growth in Canada's production capacity.
"Export volumes should continue to grow strongly, in light of the high level of competitiveness of Canadian industry and an expanding U.S. economy," the board minutes said.
Consumer spending should also pick up in the last half of the year, gaining momentum from substantial job creation in recent months, the board said.
The bank reiterated its concern about the rapid growth of the narrow money supply, as measured by the aggregate M1. The year-over-year growth of M1 was about 16 percent.
The growth of M1 combined with the steepening of the yield curve "suggest economic activity will expand at a rapid pace during the next year," the bank said.
If the rapid growth of M1 persists, it may prompt inflation in the long run, the board said.
"Provided that it does not persist for too long, the rapid growth in the aggregate is not inconsistent with preserving low inflation," the board added.

The gist of the board minutes was reflected in the central bank's summer review, which was released Tuesday. The bank indicated it saw less need for easing monetary conditions as the slack in the Canadian economy shrinks.
